title: [finding] the swallow-family census's empty-worklist line still calls the #12981 gate handover "unblocked" after that handover landed
body:
A fifth stale statement in `scripts/measure-durability-swallow-family.mjs`, in the
same class as #15459 and #15473 — but this one is in the census's PRINTED OUTPUT,
not in a comment, which is why it was left alone by the PR that repaired those two
(#15502) rather than folded into it.

The empty-worklist line the report prints when tier-1 has no outstanding member
and no DETERMINED row:

```
    (none — the family is repaired; the gate handover step is unblocked)
```

The gate handover step is not "unblocked" any more — PR #15458 performed it on
2026-09-04 (`tryInsert` / `tryUpdate` are declared in the gate's
`DURABILITY_CRITICAL_CALLEES`), and #12981 closed with PR #15472. If the worklist
ever empties, the census will announce a step that already landed as if it were
still waiting for permission — the same future-tense-over-a-landed-step defect
those two cards were filed over, one layer out, in the instrument's own reading.

**Why it is not repaired in #15502:** that PR's ruling holds the census's reading
byte-identical except the gate/census OVERLAP rows it names, and this string is a
reading line. It happens not to fire on this tree (tier-1 has 1 outstanding member
in `plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts` plus 3 DETERMINED rows), so editing it would
have moved no bytes today — but the boundary is the ruling's to move, not the
dev's.

**Scope of the repair:** one string literal. Nothing else. The condition that
guards it (`byFile.size === 0 && determined.length === 0`) is correct and does not
move.

⛔ Not a behaviour defect: the census, its `--self-test` in both modes and its
controls are green, and this line is unreachable on the current tree.

Duplicate check: 561 open issues enumerated by page over the repo-scoped REST list
endpoint and grepped locally (control word verified to hit); no match. One directed
semantic search was attempted first and returned an API rate-limit error, so the
enumeration is the reading. Unassigned, unlabeled — for PM triage.
